We present the first systematic characterization of attention sparsity in autoregressive image generation across diverse workloads and representative open-source models. Our analysis reveals several distinguishing properties, including a pronounced prefill-decode asymmetry, strong attention concentration on prompt and local tokens, and a unique diagonal attention sparsity pattern arising from the spatial locality of visual tokens. Motivated by these observations, we propose a diagonal-aware sparse attention mechanism that selectively skips KV entries along the diagonal attention direction within a recent window. Implemented on top of a GPU-based serving system using FlexGen, FlashAttention-2, and custom kernels, our approach achieves up to 3.1x throughput and 1.19x latency improvements with less than 2% quality degradation compared to dense inference.

</details>


### [25] [GAPrompt++: Multi-Granular Geometry-Aware Point Cloud Prompt for 3D Vision Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19716)
*Zixiang Ai,Zhenyu Cui,Yufei Guo,Wenwen Qiang,Lei Chen,Jiwen Lu,Jiahuan Zhou*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GAPrompt++ introduces a multi-granular geometry-aware prompting framework for 3D vision model adaptation via PEFT, featuring Point Shift Prompter (multi-scale geometric features), Keypoint Prompter (point-level saliency prompts), and a Prompt Propagation mechanism. It achieves state-of-the-art results among prompting-based PEFT methods and even surpasses full fine-tuning with under 2% trainable parameters, and adds two challenging benchmarks derived from 3D Gaussian Splatting and Multi-View Stereo to address dataset saturation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Full fine-tuning of pre-trained 3D vision models is computationally heavy, and existing prompting-based PEFT methods fail to exploit intrinsic geometric structures of point clouds—lacking both fine-grained geometric cues and coarse-grained structural semantics, and ineffective propagation through the model hierarchy.

Method: A three-component approach: (1) Point Shift Prompter extracts multi-granular geometric features across scales for instance-specific geometric adjustments; (2) Keypoint Prompter adaptively generates point-level prompts to emphasize local geometry and fine-grained structure; (3) Prompt Propagation injects these multi-granular cues throughout the feature extraction hierarchy to strengthen geometric characterization.

Result: GAPrompt++ achieves state-of-the-art performance among prompting-based PEFT methods and even surpasses full fine-tuning across diverse benchmarks, while using less than 2% of trainable parameters. The authors also introduce two new challenging benchmarks derived from 3D Gaussian Splatting and Multi-View Stereo to promote further research.

Conclusion: Multi-granular, geometry-aware prompting, coupled with effective propagation, yields substantial gains for 3D PEFT, enabling efficient adaptation with minimal trainable parameters and motivating the proposed new benchmarks to challenge and advance the field.

Abstract: Pre-trained 3D vision models have substantially advanced point cloud analysis, yet adapting them to downstream tasks via full fine-tuning is computationally expensive and storage-intensive. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) offers a promising alternative by reducing both adaptation cost and storage burden. However, existing prompting-based approaches ignore the intrinsic geometric structures of point clouds, thereby limiting their adaptation capability. This limitation stems from their inability to encode both fine-grained geometric cues and coarse-grained structural semantics, as well as failing to propagate such information effectively through the model hierarchy. To address these challenges, we propose GAPrompt++, a multi-granular geometry-aware prompting method that provides richer geometric guidance for efficient 3D task adaptation. Specifically, we introduce a Point Shift Prompter that extracts multi-granular geometric features across different scales, enabling instance-specific geometric adjustments during adaptation. Next, a Keypoint Prompter adaptively generates point-level prompts to highlight local geometric saliency and fine-grained structural details. Furthermore, a Prompt Propagation mechanism injects these multi-granular geometric cues throughout the feature extraction hierarchy, strengthening the ability to capture essential geometric characteristics. Extensive experiments show that GAPrompt++ achieves state-of-the-art performance among prompting-based PEFT methods and even surpasses full fine-tuning across diverse benchmarks, while requiring less than 2\% trainable parameters. In addition, to address the saturation of existing evaluation datasets, we construct two more challenging benchmarks derived from 3D Gaussian Splatting and Multi-View Stereo reconstruction, offering diverse and realistic point cloud scenarios to promote future research.

</details>


### [26] [SeetaPsych v1.0: An Open-source Computer Vision Toolkit for Behavior-based Psychological Measurement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19719)
*Jiabei Zeng,Chiqin Li,Kaizhou Li,Fei Chang,Yong Li,Yuanhao Zhao,Dan Han,Wenqiang Yang,Xilin Chen,Shiguang Shan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SeetaPsych v1.0 is an open-source, unified CV toolkit that integrates face-based emotion analysis, heart rate estimation, screen gaze, and scene gaze with preprocessing and a modular pipeline, providing Python APIs and a WebUI for scalable behavioral psychology research.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Fragmented, task-specific CV modules hinder reproducibility and large-scale behavioral analysis. A unified, extensible toolkit reduces integration overhead and accelerates psychology and HCI research.

Method: A modular Pipeline/Runner architecture that resolves attribute dependencies and builds computation graphs. Four core modules: (1) unified face-based emotion analysis (FER, AU detection, valence–arousal), (2) camera-based heart rate estimation, (3) screen point-of-gaze estimation, (4) scene gaze following; plus preprocessing modules (face/landmark/head detection). Standardized Python APIs and an interactive WebUI enable reproducible, large-scale analyses and rapid method evaluation.

Result: Release includes four core modules and auxiliary preprocessing; provides an integrated and extensible platform with standardized APIs and WebUI, supporting reproducible large-scale behavior-cognition research across psychology, behavioral science, HCI, etc.

Conclusion: SeetaPsych offers an integrated, accessible visual measurement platform that consolidates facial expression, physiology, and gaze analytics for psychology and related fields.

Abstract: Automated visual analysis opens new avenues for behavior--based psychological measurement. Nevertheless, existing technological modules are typically scattered across task specific systems with heterogeneous interfaces and disparate deployment requirements. In this work, we present SeetaPsych v1.0, an open source, unified and extensible computer vision toolkit designed to extract psychologically relevant signals from facial images and/or face based videos. The current release encompasses four major core modules aiming at behavior--based physiological perception: unified face based emotion analysis (simultaneous facial expression recognition, facial action unit detection, and valence--arousal estimation), camera based heart rate estimation, screen point--of--gaze estimation, and scene gaze following. A suite of auxiliary preprocessing modules for human centric visual analysis is also included, comprising face detection, facial landmark detection, and head detection. These functionalities are encapsulated within a modular Pipeline/Runner architecture that automatically resolves attribute dependencies, constructs computation graphs, and support intermediate result sharing among modules. SeetaPsych provides standardized Python APIs to facilitate reproducible, large scale analyses, alongside an interactive WebUI for rapid, code--free method evaluation. Overall, SeetaPsych offers an integrated and accessible visual measurement platform for research in psychology, behavioral science, human computer interaction, and related fields.

</details>


### [27] [Recency Forcing: Bridging the Long-Horizon Gap in Autoregressive Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19729)
*Tri Cao,Hung Nguyen,Phong Nguyen,Khoi Nguyen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Recency Forcing mitigates train-inference KV eviction mismatch in autoregressive video generation by decoupling distant context influence via Temporal Response Bias and BAR, achieving state-of-the-art long-horizon results without extra inference cost.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Train-inference discrepancy arises because models are trained on full KV-context for short clips but must operate with eviction of distant frames during inference due to memory constraints. Context truncation degrades motion coherence; a method that preserves context while reducing distant influence is needed.

Method: Define a positional response R(Δ, t_denoise) to quantify how context influence decays with temporal distance. Propose Temporal Response Bias (TRB), a non-positive, timestep-dependent bias on pre-softmax attention logits, derived from R. Introduce Biased Attention Reparameterization (BAR) to move the bias outside the softmax, enabling zero-overhead integration via FlashAttention. Recency Forcing can operate in both training-free and training-based modes.

Result: Experiments on VBench and VBench-Long show state-of-the-art long-horizon generation quality with no additional inference cost, validating effectiveness in preserving long-range coherence without increasing compute.

Conclusion: The approach closes the train-inference gap without altering context length or training objectives, delivering efficient, high-quality long-horizon AR video generation and suggesting broader applicability to sequence models with limited memory.

Abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video generation degrades over long horizons due to an overlooked train-inference discrepancy we term KV eviction mismatch: models train on short clips where all context frames reside in the KV cache, but at inference, memory constraints force distant frames to be evicted from the KV cache - removing context the model was conditioned on. Rather than simulating eviction via context truncation - which discards temporal information the model still needs and degrades motion coherence - we keep the context but while progressively reducing the influence of distant frames, making their eventual eviction negligible. To guide this design, we introduce the positional response $R( Δ, \, t_{\text{denoise}})$, a perturbation-based sensitivity measure revealing that context influence decays steeply with temporal distance and varies systematically across denoising steps. Motivated by this analysis, we propose Recency Forcing, which applies a non-positive, timestep-dependent bias, termed Temporal Response Bias (TRB), on pre-softmax attention logits derived directly from $R$, closing the train-inference gap without modifying context length or training objectives. We further introduce Biased Attention Reparameterization (BAR), an exact reformulation that moves the bias outside the softmax, making TRB a standard FlashAttention call at zero overhead. Recency Forcing operates in both training-free mode and training-based mode. Experiments on VBench and VBench-Long demonstrate state-of-the-art long-horizon generation quality at no additional inference cost.

</details>


### [28] [Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Kidney Stone Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19740)
*Najiyya Younas,Omar Abdulkader,Yaser Ali Shah,Muhammad Jawad Ikram,Jebran Khan,Amaad Khalil*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Federated YOLOv8 for kidney stone detection on CT preserves patient privacy while achieving competitive object-detection performance and enabling real-time edge deployment in a distributed setting.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address privacy and data-security concerns in medical imaging by enabling collaborative model training without sharing patient data, in compliance with GDPR/HIPAA.

Method: Integrate Federated Learning with an optimized YOLOv8 for kidney stone detection on CT images; incorporate residual feature fusion and DropBlock regularization; operate on distributed CT datasets to enable privacy-preserving training and edge-friendly inference.

Result: mAP@50 of 0.733 on a distributed CT dataset; demonstrates data confidentiality and suitability for fast edge deployment with real-time inference in clinical settings.

Conclusion: Federated Learning combined with advanced object-detection architectures (e.g., YOLOv8 with architectural refinements) is a viable and efficient approach for privacy-preserving AI-assisted diagnosis in healthcare.

Abstract: Recent innovations in deep learning have significantly enhanced the diagnosis of medical images, although they are based on the use of centralized data storage that pose severe threats to patient privacy and medical data security. To address this issue, this research proposes a Federated Learning (FL) model that is coupled with an optimized YOLOv8 network to detect the kidney stones on a computed tomography (CT) image and at the same time, protect privacy of the patients. The suggested system can help various medical organizations to jointly train a common model without exchanging the information about the patients. This is to ensure that data protection laws like GDPR and HIPAA are adhered to. The residual feature fusion and DropBlock regularization among other architectural improvements are also included in YOLOv8 to enhance detection robustness and minimize overfitting. Experimental analysis carried out on a distributed CT dataset demonstrated that the federated YOLOv8 model has a mAP at 50 of 0.733 and is able to keep the data confidential. Moreover, its lean design facilitates fast edge deployment and real-time inference across a clinical setting. Altogether, these findings indicate that Federated Learning is a safe and efficient solution to AI-assisted diagnosis in contemporary healthcare when combined with the use of sophisticated object detection models.

</details>


### [29] [Region-Level Policy Optimization for Fine-grained MLLM Perception](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19745)
*Yuheng Shi,Xiaohuan Pei,Minjing Dong,Chang Xu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Vision-RL2 trains a region-level RL-based proposal network to select RoIs for fine-grained perception in MLLMs, achieving higher accuracy with substantially fewer visual tokens across benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To reduce the token and computation burden of high-resolution visual encoding in MLLMs by exploiting distinct resolution needs for localization and recognition, enabling coarse-to-fine RoI localization that preserves evidence while cutting token usage.

Method: Introduce Vision-RL2: treat coherent regions as actions in region-level reinforcement learning. A frozen MLLM reader scores each region by how removing it changes answer likelihood. Train the proposal predictor with region-level RL and complementary subtractive/additive objectives to suppress distractors and recover missing evidence, updating only the predictor without region annotations or reasoning trajectories. The RoI proposals enable sparse encoding and focus on evidence.

Result: Across six fine-grained benchmarks and four MLLM backbones, Vision-RL2 improves accuracy over the base model at every token budget and surpasses the base model’s largest-budget accuracy with ~4× fewer visual tokens. Code available at the provided GitHub link.

Conclusion: Vision-RL2 provides an effective, efficient approach for fine-grained perception in MLLMs by learning a faithfulness-aware RoI proposal network that concentrates evidence, reduces visual-token costs, and maintains or improves accuracy across settings.

Abstract: Fine-grained visual perception in MLLMs is commonly improved by raising the resolution, but the added visual tokens inflate vision-encoding and language-model prefilling costs. We show that the two operations underlying fine-grained perception, localizing the region of interest (RoI) and recognizing its content, have different resolution requirements. In a controlled diagnostic, localization tolerates roughly 3 to 4 times stronger token compression than recognition, which motivates localizing from a coarse view and concentrating resolution on the selected evidence. Decoding coordinates with the MLLM can be trained end-to-end from answers, but costs a full model pass per query and depends on grounding ability. A lightweight proposal network distilled from the model's attention is fast, but inherits the noise of its attention targets. The RoI from the proposal network reaches the answer through a discrete region choice, so its faithfulness to the answer cannot supervise the network. We therefore optimize the proposal network with region-level reinforcement learning, which we call Vision-RL2. It treats coherent regions as actions, and a frozen MLLM reader scores each one by how its removal changes the answer likelihood. Complementary subtractive and additive objectives suppress distracting proposals and recover missing evidence, updating only the predictor without region annotations, response sampling, or reasoning trajectories. The refined proposal further enables a sparse encoding that magnifies evidence and excludes background tokens. Across six fine-grained benchmarks and four MLLM backbones, Vision-RL2 improves accuracy over the base model at every token budget and surpasses its largest-budget accuracy with about 4 times fewer visual tokens. Code is available at https://github.com/YuHengsss/VisionRL2 .

</details>


### [30] [STAR: Structure-aware Test-time Adaptation for diffusion-based light field Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19747)
*Wontae Choi,Ki Ryum Moon,Jae Young Lee,Hyung Sup Yun,Il Yong Chun*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: STAR adapts diffusion priors at test time with three lightweight adapters to reconstruct light fields from focal stacks, addressing scene-specific spatial-angular structure.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: LF reconstruction from limited/noisy focal stack measurements is highly ill-posed. A fixed pre-trained prior cannot capture the varying spatial-angular structure (within-view details, cross-view angular dependencies, and disparity) across scenes, motivating test-time adaptation.

Method: Freeze a pre-trained diffusion prior and fit three lightweight adapters to the observed focal stack to jointly adapt the LF's three components of spatial-angular structure, enabling structure-aware reconstruction at test time.

Result: STAR outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both two- and three-focal-sheet settings, with shorter inference times than approaches that perform test-time parameter updates.

Conclusion: STAR is the first test-time adaptation framework for LF reconstruction from focal stacks, introducing efficient, structure-aware adaptation that improves reconstruction quality while reducing inference time.

Abstract: Light field (LF) reconstruction from limited and noisy focal stack (FS) measurements is a highly ill-posed inverse problem. Although the LF-to-FS imaging geometry is fixed for a given optical setup, LF spatial-angular structure---including within-view spatial details, cross-view angular dependencies, and disparity across views---varies across scenes. Consequently, a fixed pre-trained prior may not optimally capture the spatial-angular structure of each test LF. We propose Structure-aware Test-time Adaptation for diffusion-based light field Reconstruction (STAR), the first test-time adaptation framework for reconstructing an LF from FS. For each test LF, STAR freezes a pre-trained diffusion prior and fits three lightweight adapters to the observed FS to jointly adapt the three components of the LF's spatial-angular structure. STAR outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both two- and three-focal-sheet settings, with shorter inference times than those with test-time parameter updates.

</details>


### [31] [Benchmarking MLLMs via Cognitive Expected Scene Graph for Safety-Critical Visual Negation Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19767)
*Zhiyun Jiang,Hanyong Wang,Binbin Liang,Yu Xie,Menglong Yang,Wei Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces SNUS (Scene Negation Understanding under Safety Cognition) and CESG, a negative-caption dataset and a polarity-aware, structure-grounded metric, to address risk-aware negation in vision-language models; findings show current models fail on negation and standard metrics collapse under semantic reversals, with the framework providing a robust SNUS benchmark.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the lack of robust, meaningful negation understanding in vision-language systems by anchoring negation reasoning to safety-oriented cognitive goals, reducing open-ended, biased evaluation of negation.

Method: Define the SNUS task; construct a high-fidelity negative caption dataset that maps dense hazard assertions; propose the Cognitive Expected Scene Graph (CESG) Score as a polarity-aware, structure-grounded evaluation metric; conduct extensive experiments comparing models and metrics on SNUS.

Result: Demonstrates that current models struggle with SNUS; traditional metrics collapse when semantics are reversed; the proposed CESG-based evaluation provides a stable benchmark, and the dataset enables rigorous risk-aware scene understanding and counterfactual cognition.

Conclusion: SNUS, with CESG, offers a rigorous framework and benchmark for safe, risk-aware visual understanding of negation, guiding future development toward more reliable counterfactual and safety-conscious cognition.

Abstract: True machine intelligence requires transcending passive pixel registration to master top-down functional reasoning over absent information via visual negation understanding. However, unconstrained visual negation paradigms remain overly open-ended, and pervasive affirmation bias causes both existing Multi-Modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and evaluation metrics to fail under negative semantics. To solve these intertwined challenges systematically, we first anchor the boundaries of negation reasoning within specific cognitive goals. Specifically, by focusing on safety as a highly pragmatic and critical cognitive dimension, we define the task of \textbf{S}cene \textbf{N}egation \textbf{U}nderstanding under \textbf{S}afety Cognition (\textbf{SNUS}). Under this framework, we construct a high-fidelity negative caption dataset mapping dense assertions of localized hazards. Concurrently, we propose the Cognitive Expected Scene Graph (CESG) Score, a structure-grounded, polarity-aware evaluation metric. Extensive experiments demonstrate that while current models struggle on the task, traditional metrics completely collapse under semantic reversals. Conversely, our framework delivers a solid benchmark for SNUS, providing a rigorous foundation to advance risk-aware situational comprehension and counterfactual cognition.

</details>


### [32] [AI Smart Glasses for Wearable Intelligence: From Egocentric Sensing to Agentic Personalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19793)
*Xu Yuan,Yi Wang,Zhuohang Jiang,Haohao Qu,Yujuan Ding,Shanru Lin,Guoliang Xing,Hongxia Yang,Jiannong Cao,Qing Li,Wenqi Fan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Defines AI smart glasses as a system-level wearable-intelligence platform and surveys a four-dimension framework (hardware, wearable intelligence, interaction, applications) with five cross-cutting challenges to guide design and evaluation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To unify design, evaluation, and research directions for AI-enabled smart glasses by framing them as a holistic wearable-intelligence system.

Method: Survey-based framework analyzing four interconnected dimensions (hardware, wearable intelligence, interaction design, application scenarios) and identifying five cross-cutting research challenges; organizes material by domain requirements and deployment constraints.

Result: A cohesive conceptual model and framework for AI smart glasses, outlining core components, interaction modalities, and application areas, plus a roadmap of challenges: hardware, trustworthy egocentric intelligence, lifelong personalized memory, proactive intelligence, and embodied foundation models.

Conclusion: Centering smart glasses as wearable-intelligence platforms provides a unified lens for technology development, application deployment, and evaluation in this emerging field.

Abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping smart glasses from egocentric capture and display devices into platforms for wearable intelligence. Smart glasses increasingly serve as wearable AI systems that connect first-person observation with real-time assistance under strict form-factor constraints. We frame this transition through the lens of \emph{AI smart glasses} and define them as a system-level concept in which egocentric sensing, resource-aware computing, intelligent reasoning, multimodal interaction, and real-world application constraints are co-designed for personalized assistance in the physical world. To systematically study this perspective, we organize the survey around four connected dimensions. First, we examine the hardware foundation that bounds sensing, computation, feedback delivery, and sustained deployment. Second, we study wearable intelligence, where egocentric signals are transformed into perceptual, contextual, and agentic capabilities. Third, we discuss interaction design, through which users request, receive, correct, and regulate assistance during ongoing activity. Fourth, we analyze application scenarios across healthcare, accessibility, situated learning, daily life assistance, cultural tourism, and industrial support, showing how domain requirements reshape system design and evaluation. We further identify five cross-cutting research challenges for future AI smart glasses: next-generation hardware, trustworthy egocentric intelligence, lifelong personalized memory, proactive intelligence, and embodied foundation models. By centering smart glasses as wearable-intelligence platforms, this survey provides a unified framework for organizing technologies, applications, and open challenges in this emerging area.

</details>


### [33] [Absence is Presence: Understanding Visual Scene Negative Events Under Safety Cognitive Constraint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19812)
*Zhiyun Jiang,Hanyong Wang,Binbin Liang,Yu Xie,Menglong Yang,Wei Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CRCD is a counterfactual reconstruction and contrastive decoding framework for negative captioning that identifies safety-relevant omissions in scenes. It uses a dual-branch architecture (amodal completion and functional association), plus multi-condition representation learning, and decodes semantic residuals between reconstructed prototypes and the input to trigger negative reasoning, achieving strong empirical results and establishing a baseline for safety-focused negative captioning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: In safety-critical domains, negations (absences) of expected safety objects are crucial for risk mitigation, but standard vision-language models suffer from affirmation bias and representation gaps when inferring non-existence.

Method: Proposes counterfactual latent change captioning (CRCD) that bypasses affirmation bias by contrasting a synthesized safe expectation with reality. Introduces a dual-branch counterfactual reconstruction architecture: (1) amodal completion to restore partially visible objects and (2) functional association to infer completely absent safety objects. Employs multi-condition representation learning to project universal features onto predefined safety subspaces. Decodes feature-level semantic residuals between a reconstructed scene prototype and the raw input to bound the search space for non-existence and trigger negative logic.

Result: Extensive experiments validate the approach and establish a high-performance baseline for visual scene negative captioning under safety constraints.

Conclusion: CRCD provides a principled, practical framework for reasoning about absences in images under safety constraints, addressing affirmation bias and representation bias, with demonstrated empirical effectiveness and potential for broader safety-critical applications.

Abstract: Traditional scene understanding focuses on affirmative information objectively present in images. However, in safety-critical domains, comprehending key information that should exist but is actually absent is vital for risk mitigation. To bridge this gap, we focus on visual scene negative captioning with safety as the cognitive constraint. The core challenge is to convert physical absence into semantic negative events. Existing vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with this process because affirmation bias suppresses negative reasoning, while limited mental filling capability and representation bias further hinder the inference of absent information. To address these challenges, we propose a negative captioning framework based on counterfactual reconstruction and contrastive decoding (CRCD). Inspired by human cognition, CRCD reformulates the task as counterfactual latent change captioning to bypass affirmation bias. It contrasts a synthesized safe expectation with reality to identify semantic omissions. To address limited mental filling, we design a dual-branch counterfactual reconstruction architecture. The amodal completion branch restores defective objects, while the functional association branch infers completely absent safety objects. Concurrently, a multi-condition representation learning mechanism is integrated to mitigate representation bias by projecting universal features onto predefined safety criteria subspaces, thereby capturing information across more dimensions. By decoding feature-level semantic residuals between the reconstructed scene prototype and raw input, CRCD bounds the non-existence search space and activates the decoder's negative logic. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of CRCD, establishing a high-performance baseline for this pioneering task.

</details>


### [34] [SnapPhysics: A Physics-Aware Scene Graph from a Single View for Interactive Mixed Reality Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19815)
*Suji Kang,Seok-Young Kim,Young Bin Kim,Taewook Ha,Dieter Schmalstieg,Shohei Mori,Woontack Woo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A training-free framework to reconstruct 3D objects and estimate physical properties (mass, friction, center of gravity) from a single image, using a physics-aware scene graph to ground VLM-based reasoning; shows notable gains on 3D-FRONT and real scenes versus VLM-only methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Physically coherent interactive MR requires both accurate geometry and physically grounded properties. Prior single-image approaches via VLMs lack grounding, while video-based methods are costly. A training-free, geometry-grounded property reasoning framework could enable practical MR interactions.

Method: Integrates instance-level 3D reconstruction and spatial alignment with a physics-aware scene graph that encodes inter-object relationships and per-object metric geometry as structured context for VLM-based property reasoning; operates without explicit property-specific training.

Result: On 3D-FRONT: scene-level F-Score improves by 18.6% over the best learning-based method. On real captured scenes with ground-truth mass: mean absolute log difference error (mALDE) reduced by up to 20.5%, and log-scale correlation r^2_ls improved by up to 19.6% relative to VLM-only estimation.

Conclusion: SnapPhysics enables physically interactive MR experiences without manual parameter tuning and demonstrates strong performance gains in grounding physical properties from single images.

Abstract: We propose SnapPhysics, a training-free framework that reconstructs 3D objects and estimates their physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of gravity from a single image. For physically coherent interactions in mixed reality (MR), such properties are as important as geometry. Prior approaches infer them by analyzing object dynamics in video, which is computationally costly, or by querying vision-language models (VLMs) on single images, which lacks geometric grounding and inter-object relationships. We address these limitations by combining instance-level 3D reconstruction and spatial alignment with a physics-aware scene graph that encodes these relationships and per-object metric geometry as structured context for VLM-based property reasoning. Experiments on 3D-FRONT show that SnapPhysics improves scene-level F-Score by 18.6% over the best learning-based method, and on real captured scenes with ground-truth mass, it reduces the mean absolute log difference error (mALDE) by up to 20.5% and improves log-scale correlation ($r^2_{\mathrm{ls}}$) by up to 19.6% over VLM-only estimation. SnapPhysics enables physically interactive MR experiences without manual parameter tuning. Project page: https://snapphysics-ismar2026.github.io/.

</details>


### [35] [KoUniTalk: A Lightweight Articulation-Centered Korean-English 3D Talking Face Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19840)
*Hyunjung Chung,Unsang Park*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: KoUniTalk: a lightweight Korean-English 3D talking-face benchmark retargeted to a shared 1,176-vertex template for articulation-focused cross-language evaluation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address English-centric 3D talking-face datasets and mismatches in mesh topology, spatial scale, coordinate systems, and temporal sampling between VOCASET and Korean data, enabling controlled cross-language speech-driven facial animation.

Method: Deformation-transfer retargeting to a canonical 1,176-vertex mouth-focused template (3,528D); creation of an identity-neutral output space; dimensionality reduction to 3,528 dimensions; evaluation of semantic mouth-landmark trajectories; definition of a subject-disjoint Korean benchmark split; processed benchmark: 22 speakers, 4,978 sequences, 642,781 frames.

Result: Produces a compact articulation-template space enabling Korean-English cross-dataset evaluation of speech-driven 3D facial animation models; dimensionality reduced by factors of 4.27 (vs VOCASET/FLAME) and 20.45 (vs original Korean mesh); overall dataset encompasses 22 speakers and ~643k frames.

Conclusion: KoUniTalk provides a unified, low-dimensional articulation space for cross-language speech-driven 3D facial animation research, without introducing a new deformation-transfer algorithm or a full-head avatar dataset; includes a subject-disjoint Korean benchmark and separated inventory counts.

Abstract: High-quality 3D talking face datasets remain largely English- centric, and Korean 3D facial motion data are difficult to combine with standard English benchmarks because of differences in mesh topology, spatial scale, coordinate system, and temporal sampling. We present KoUniTalk, a lightweight articulation-centered Korean-English 3D talk- ing face benchmark that retargets VOCASET and the released Korean speech-based 3D talking face data to a shared mesh topology using de- formation transfer. Rather than proposing a new deformation-transfer algorithm or a full-head identity-preserving avatar dataset, KoUniTalk provides an identity-neutral canonical output space for controlled speech- driven facial articulation training and evaluation across English and Ko- rean. The unified template contains 1,176 vertices and focuses on the mouth and adjacent lower- and mid-face regions, reducing the output dimensionality from 15,069 and 72,147 dimensions to 3,528 dimensions, corresponding to 4.27-fold and 20.45-fold reductions compared with VO- CASET/FLAME and the original Korean mesh, respectively. To exam- ine whether retargeting preserves speech-relevant motion, we evaluate semantic mouth-landmark trajectories, including mouth opening, mouth width, aperture ratio, and mouth-opening dynamics. Since the official test set of the Korean dataset is not publicly released, we additionally define a subject-disjoint Korean benchmark split. The processed matched benchmark contains 22 speakers, 4,978 sequences, and 642,781 frames, enabling Korean-English cross-dataset evaluation of speech-driven 3D fa- cial animation models in a single compact articulation-template space. Source-reported inventory counts are listed separately from these pro- cessed counts

</details>


### [36] [PACE: Precise AI Cinematic Expression: A Typed Specification for Script-Grounded Previsualization and Geometric Conformance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19853)
*Bing Duan,Qiang Guo,Linpu Li,Zhijian Mao,Min Zhu,Zhirui Ren,Yiwei Yan,Xi Chu,Xiaoding Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PACE provides a typed, hierarchical representation for cinematic planning that binds screenplay elements to precise on-set geometry and camera framing, with a compiler to generate diffusion prompts and 3D scenes and a camera solver to enforce framing.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the misalignment between written screenplay directives, diffusion-model prompts, and actual camera framing; enabling quantitative evaluation of how well declared poses map to rendered frames.

Method: Introduce PACE, a typed plan representation (script, scene, shot, panel) with inherited values; a compiler that outputs diffusion prompts and metres-scale 3D scenes; a camera solver that realizes declared framing; field-by-field error measurement between declarations and realized geometry.

Result: Empirical evaluation on 11 Automatic Drive screenplay scenes shows single-subject panels place subject near declared position with 1.2% frame-width tolerance; multi-subject panels exhibit residual pose conflicts; 204 external shots show head height deviations depending on words, prompt, or greybox; declaring poses increases action conformity from 58.9% to 74.4% without changing framing.

Conclusion: PACE yields more faithful realization of declared cinematic plans and enables quantitative diagnostics of deviations; code is available (GitHub) but transitions, motion fitting, and human review remain open research areas.

Abstract: Between a screenplay and a film sits a planning problem that is spatial first: who stands where, and what a camera sees from where it stands. An image diffusion model asked for a shot in free text settles that plan by its own defaults. We present PACE (Precise AI Cinematic Expression), a typed representation for the plan: the screenplay evidence, the characters, props and locations it needs, where each subject stands, and what the camera does. A value is written once at the level it belongs to (script, scene, shot or panel) and inherited below it. A compiler turns the result into both the prompt sent to the diffusion model and a 3D scene built in metres, and a camera solver places the camera so that the declared framing is the framing built. Where a declared value becomes geometry, PACE measures, field by field, how far the compiled camera and the staged render sit from the declaration, rather than asking a model to judge.
  On the 11-scene Automatic Drive screenplay, every staged single-subject panel places its subject within 1.2% of frame width of its declared position; with two or three subjects one camera pose cannot satisfy every position, and the residual is reported rather than absorbed. On 204 external director-storyboard shots, delivered head height is 1.906 times the staged target from the director's words, 1.733 from the compiled prompt, and 0.955 with the greybox control; the condition that holds framing best draws the described action least. Declaring the pose on 30 shots raises the action drawn from 58.9% to 74.4% without moving the framing. Transitions, fitted motion and human review of the generated panels remain open. Code: https://github.com/StudioPiLabs/pace-core

</details>


### [37] [Socialized UAV Cross-Task Learning: Towards Cross-Granularity Collaboration through Hierarchical Interaction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19867)
*Xinjie Yao,Ruipu Zhao,Yunqi Zhu,Zhihe Fan,Zhoupeng Guo,Weihao Li,Zhen Wang,Qilong Wang,Pengfei Zhu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CrossUAV introduces a benchmark and CGSC framework for joint object detection and instance segmentation across coarse- and fine-grained representations, addressing cross-granularity interference via hierarchical interaction regulation, yielding consistent gains.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Cross-task learning with mismatched granularity often causes interference, bias, or collapse; UAV perception inherently spans coarse (detection) and fine (segmentation) cues requiring regulated cross-talk.

Method: CGSC progressively activates cross-task interactions and adaptively modulates exchange strength across network hierarchies based on task contribution; the CrossUAV benchmark provides a unified evaluation platform for cross-granularity collaboration.

Result: Empirical results show consistent improvements on both detection and segmentation tasks, validating hierarchical dynamic interaction as an effective mechanism for cross-granularity collaboration.

Conclusion: Regulating hierarchical cross-task interactions is crucial for cross-granularity learning; CGSC is effective, and the CrossUAV benchmark facilitates robust evaluation.

Abstract: Joint learning across heterogeneous tasks is often treated as task coupling through feature sharing, distillation, or auxiliary supervision. However, in cross-task learning, mismatched representational and supervisory granularities make such coupling prone to interference, teacher bias, or unidirectional collapse. We argue that cross-granularity learning is fundamentally a problem of hierarchical interaction regulation rather than simple task coupling. This issue is particularly evident in UAV perception, where visual shifts and detection--segmentation objectives naturally form coarse- and fine-grained knowledge sources. To systematically study this problem, we introduce CrossUAV, a UAV benchmark for joint object detection and instance segmentation that provides a unified evaluation platform for cross-granularity task collaboration. To address these challenges, we propose Cross-Granularity Socialized Collaboration (CGSC), a progressive and adaptive framework that regulates when, where, and how tasks exchange information across network hierarchies. CGSC progressively activates cross-task interactions and adaptively adjusts the strength according to task contribution, suppressing harmful interference while exploiting complementary coarse- and fine-grained structures. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements on both tasks, validating hierarchical dynamic interaction as an effective mechanism for cross-granularity collaboration.

</details>


### [38] [PART: Learning 3D Part Assembly and Retrieval with Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19872)
*Ruchao Bao,Wenzheng Wu,Chucheng Xiang,Zhongyuan Liu,Yuan Liu,Jinxin Dong,Ligang Liu,Ziqi Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PART is a transformer-based framework that retrieves 3D parts and predicts their 6-DoF poses to assemble a target from a library, addressing combinatorial search, variable-length outputs, and continuous pose estimation via set prediction and segmentation-enhanced optimization; demonstrated on a large 80k+ shape dataset with cross-modal generalization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enable practical, retrieval-based 3D part assembly by overcoming the limitations of prior work that handles only predefined parts, specifically the exponential search space, variable part counts, and continuous 6-DoF pose estimation.

Method: A unified transformer-based set-prediction framework that jointly retrieves parts and regresses their 6-DoF poses for the target. It leverages a segmentation-augmented optimization module and exploits the duality between pose estimation and segmentation through joint training, along with a large-scale 80k+ shape dataset.

Result: PART demonstrates generalization to scene layouts, image targets, and real-world scans, indicating robustness across modalities and settings.

Conclusion: The work advances practical 3D assembly by unifying retrieval and pose estimation in a single transformer framework, enabling variable-length outputs and continuous 6-DoF predictions, and introduces a large-scale dataset and segmentation-enhanced optimization to improve performance.

Abstract: 3D assembly is fundamental to modern manufacturing and digital content creation. In this paper, we present PART, a unified transformer-based framework for 3D part retrieval and assembly: given a target shape and a part library, PART automatically selects the appropriate parts and predicts their 6-DoF poses to reconstruct the target. While prior work has achieved impressive progress on assembling a pre-defined set of parts, this more practical retrieval-based setting remains largely unexplored. The task faces three key challenges: (i) a combinatorially explosive search space that grows exponentially with library size; (ii) variable-length outputs, as different targets require different numbers of parts; and (iii) continuous 6-DoF pose estimation for part assembly. To address these, we formulate retrieval and assembly as a set prediction problem and design a novel transformer-based framework that retrieves parts and regresses their poses with variable-length output. Additionally, we exploit the duality between part pose estimation and target segmentation through joint training and a novel segmentation-enhanced optimization module. Finally, We curate a large-scale dataset of 80K+ shapes, and the results show that PART generalizes to scene layouts, image targets, and real-world scans. Project Page: https://iambrc.github.io/PART-project-page/.

</details>


### [39] [BINDER: A Latent Variable Model for Probabilistic Medical Image Registration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19875)
*Stefano Cerri,Amirhossein Hassankhani,Yaël Balbastre,Koen Van Leemput*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Bayesian deformable registration (BINDER) introduces latent voxel correspondences into MI-based registration, yielding closed-form updates, a demons-like nonlinear optimizer, and a uncertainty-quantifying sampler for high-dimensional 3D multimodal registrations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To achieve robust, general-purpose medical image registration with explicit uncertainty quantification, particularly for multimodal and high-dimensional 3D data, extending mutual information-based approaches with a probabilistic framework.

Method: A probabilistic model built on mutual information that uses latent voxel-wise correspondences. It derives closed-form iterative updates for optimization and MCMC sampling. Produces a demons-like nonlinear registration algorithm and a Bayesian sampler capable of quantifying uncertainty in high-dimensional 3D deformations. Implemented in BINDER, an open-source toolkit.

Result: Demonstrates robust out-of-the-box performance across mono- and multimodal registration tasks. The uncertainty sampler enables quantification of registration uncertainty in high-dimensional 3D deformations. Code is publicly available at the provided GitHub URL.

Conclusion: BINDER provides a principled Bayesian framework for deformable registration that delivers accurate, robust performance and explicit uncertainty estimation in challenging multimodal and high-dimensional 3D settings, with an open-source implementation.

Abstract: We propose a new probabilistic model for general-purpose medical image registration that builds upon the mutual information registration criterion. It centers around a spatial interpolation technique that assumes latent voxel-wise correspondences between the images being registered. By exploiting these latent variables, we derive dedicated optimization and MCMC sampling techniques that only involve closed-form iterative updates. When applied to nonlinear registration, an efficient demons-like optimization algorithm is obtained that shows robust out-of-the-box performance across a variety of monomodal and multimodal registration tasks. We also demonstrate a corresponding sampler that can quantify, for the first time, uncertainty in multimodal registration scenarios with very high-dimensional 3D deformations. Our code, which we call BINDER (Bayesian INference for DEformable Registration), is freely available at https://github.com/ste93ste/BINDER.

</details>


### [40] [SlugTrails: An Egocentric Benchmark for Floor Plan Localization in Large Buildings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19876)
*Yunqian Cheng,Roberto Manduchi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SlugTrails is a large-scale, floor-plan localization benchmark for egocentric, indoor localization in big campuses, with CAD floor plans, laser-aligned trajectories, and three practical sensing protocols. Stock model weights underperform; fine-tuning yields large gains across methods and tasks, and improves cross-dataset generalization (LaMAR). The work highlights data limitation over model capacity and releases data/tools for community use.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Bridge the gap between small-scale residential benchmarks and real-world, large indoor deployments. Provide standardized protocols, realistic sensing, and precise ground truth to evaluate geometry-based localizers on large spaces.

Method: Data collection of 30 Hz Aria glasses across three campus buildings and six floors, using CAD floor plans with semantic classes and circulation masks; trajectories aligned to floor plans with laser-surveyed anchors; three protocols: single walking frame, stationary multi-view sweep, walking stream with odometry; evaluation of five geometric/learned systems under native sensing.

Result: Stock checkpoints perform near zero on SlugTrails; fine-tuning on SlugTrails substantially improves all trainable methods (e.g., F^3Loc 0.0→0.141 on single-frame; 0.03→0.66 sequential); gains compound with observations; improved cross-dataset generalization to LaMAR (sequential R@1m: 0.048→0.143 for F^3Loc, 0.063→0.127 for UnLoc); train-from-scratch on SlugTrails remains weak; evidence that indoor data limitations, not architecture, limit performance.

Conclusion: SlugTrails offers a realistic, large-scale benchmark with protocols and tools, revealing the importance of data adaptation and fine-tuning for floor-plan localization. The dataset enables fair cross-dataset evaluation and highlights data quality as a key bottleneck; authors release data and tools.

Abstract: Floor-plan-based indoor visual localization enables infrastructure-free positioning, but most methods are developed and evaluated in small residential environments unlike the large public buildings of real deployment. We introduce SlugTrails, a floor plan localization benchmark for large indoor spaces under realistic egocentric sensing: $30$ Hz Aria glasses recordings across three campus buildings and six floors ($22089$ m$^2$ of floor plan outline), CAD-derived floor plans with semantic classes and circulation space masks, and trajectories aligned into the floor plan frame using laser-surveyed anchors. One protocol covers three practical ways of gathering geometry under a limited field of view -- a single walking frame, a stationary multi-view sweep, and a walking stream with odometry -- so methods designed for different regimes are compared on the same buildings and ground truth. Evaluating five representative geometric and learned systems under their native sensing configurations, we find that stock checkpoints (official released weights) are near zero on SlugTrails (at most $0.004$ R@1m30$^{\circ}$ on walking single frames), while fine-tuning on SlugTrails improves every trainable family on all three tasks (e.g., F$^3$Loc $0.0 \rightarrow 0.141$ single-frame and $0.03 \rightarrow 0.66$ sequential), with gains compounding as observations accumulate. The same fine-tuned weights also improve cross-dataset generalization on LaMAR with no LaMAR training (sequential R@1m $0.048 \rightarrow 0.143$ for F$^3$Loc and $0.063 \rightarrow 0.127$ for UnLoc), whereas train-from-scratch on SlugTrails alone stays far below fine-tuning from stock weights -- evidence that floor plan localization is currently limited by indoor data rather than by architecture. We release the dataset, protocols, and tools at https://github.com/Head-inthe-Cloud/SlugTrails.

</details>


### [41] [BinoGen: Scaling egocentric binocular data for embodied visual perception and learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19881)
*Chunpeng Li,Ya-tang Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: BinoGen is an automated framework that generates large-scale, embodiment-aware egocentric binocular visual data and demonstrates that embodiment-aware training improves real-world perception and enables cross-embodiment learning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the data scarcity and cost of collecting large-scale, annotated, egocentric binocular data, and study how observer embodiment (height, FOV, binocular geometry, motion) shapes perceptual learning.

Method: Generative scene synthesis with probabilistic object instantiation, appearance randomization, stochastic trajectory generation, and configurable binocular camera setups to create synchronized binocular videos plus dense multimodal supervision (depth, optical flow, surface normals, semantic maps, object coordinates, camera poses).

Result: Built a dataset of over 20 million annotated images; demonstrated that BinoGen data improves real-world perception tasks (depth estimation, object detection, video tracking); showed that comparing human-inspired and mouse-inspired embodiments enables controlled investigation of embodiment effects, with embodiment-specific adaptation improving performance and joint training achieving cross-embodiment competitiveness.

Conclusion: Large-scale, controllable visual experiences that incorporate embodiment can significantly enhance embodied perception and support robust, adaptable models across different observer embodiments.

Abstract: Embodied visual perception relies on temporally coherent visual experience accumulated through continuous engagement with the environment. However, collecting large-scale egocentric binocular observations together with dense annotations remains costly and difficult. Moreover, visual experience is shaped not only by the environment but also by the embodiment of the observer, including viewing height, field of view, binocular geometry, and motion through the scene. To address these challenges, we present BinoGen, an automated framework for generating large-scale, embodiment-aware egocentric binocular visual experiences in indoor environments. BinoGen jointly models environmental and observer variation through generative scene synthesis, probabilistic object instantiation, appearance randomization, stochastic trajectory generation, and configurable binocular camera setups. The framework produces synchronized binocular videos together with dense multimodal supervision, including depth maps, optical flow, surface normals, semantic maps, object coordinates, and camera poses. Using BinoGen, we construct a dataset comprising more than 20 million annotated images for supervised learning. We demonstrate two complementary utilities of BinoGen. First, incorporating BinoGen data consistently improves real-world visual perception, including depth estimation, object detection, and video object tracking. Second, paired human-inspired and mouse-inspired observations from the same environments enable controlled investigation of how observer embodiment affects perceptual learning. Embodiment-specific adaptation substantially improves performance, while joint training enables a single model to perform competitively across both embodiments. Together, these results demonstrate that large-scale, controllable visual experience can improve embodied perception...

</details>


### [42] [GS-PI: An Optimization-Decoupled Appearance Decomposition Approach for Generating PBR Gaussian Assets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19907)
*Jieting Xu,Rengan Xie,Zijian Huang,Zehui Jin,Rui Wang,Yuchi Huo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GS-PI decouples illumination from geometry in Gaussian Splatting by casting PBR material generation as a geometry-conditioned 3D diffusion process, enabling relightable GS assets without per-scene joint optimization and differentiable rasterization from a point-cloud extracted from a Gaussian model.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the entanglement of lighting, materials, and geometry in Gaussian Splatting that prevents seamless integration into PBR. Existing inverse-rendering struggles with competing objectives and residual lighting artifacts.

Method: Perform a geometry-conditioned diffusion on 3D point clouds to generate PBR attributes. Operate in 3D to ensure multi-view consistency. Use multi-scale cross-view conditioning: global semantic priors, source-anchored photometric cues, and absolute spatial view-direction conditioning. Extract a point cloud from a pre-trained Gaussian model, predict PBR attributes via conditional diffusion, and distill back through differentiable rasterization to produce a relightable PBR-GS asset.

Result: GS-PI outperforms recent inverse-rendering baselines by replacing per-scene joint illumination/BRDF optimization with a learned diffusion pass followed by a short target-driven distillation, and does not require proxy meshes.

Conclusion: A geometry-conditioned diffusion framework enables effective disentanglement of lighting from geometry in GS, yielding relightable PBR-GS assets with improved multi-view consistency and reduced cross-view artifacts, suitable for integration into PBR pipelines.

Abstract: Gaussian Splatting (GS) excels at novel-view synthesis but encodes baked-in radiance, tightly entangling illumination with geometry and preventing seamless integration into physically based rendering (PBR) pipelines. Existing inverse-rendering methods attempt to disentangle materials via joint optimization, but often suffer from competing objectives that cause severe ambiguities and residual lighting artifacts. To overcome this, we present GS-PI, a novel optimization-decoupled framework that casts PBR material generation as a geometry-conditioned diffusion process on 3D point clouds. By operating directly in the 3D domain, our method inherently guarantees multi-view consistency, sidestepping the severe pixel correspondence issues that challenge 2D diffusion approaches. We introduce a multi-scale cross-view conditioning mechanism that integrates three complementary components: a global semantic prior, source-anchored photometric cues, and an absolute spatial learned view-direction conditioning signal. This design efficiently compresses complex multi-view evidence, mitigating cross-view projection misalignment and successfully preventing specular highlights from baking into intrinsic colors. By extracting a point cloud from a pre-trained Gaussian model, predicting PBR attributes via conditional diffusion, and distilling them back through differentiable rasterisation, we yield a fully relightable PBR-GS asset. GS-PI outperforms recent inverse-rendering baselines while replacing per-scene joint illumination/BRDF optimization with a learned diffusion pass followed by a short target-driven distillation, without requiring proxy meshes.

</details>


### [43] [CitySTAR: Structured and Topology-Aware Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Urban 3D Grounding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19911)
*Shuai Zhang,Hongye Hou,Qinghe Liu,Zhuoxiao Li,Dongli Wu,Jing Ou,Yuan Liu,Wufan Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Training-free, reasoning-driven framework CitySTAR for open-world city-scale 3D grounding, leveraging scene graphs and cross-modal constraints; introduces CitySTAR-3D benchmark; shows improved grounding and interpretability.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Connect natural language to implicit semantic and geometric structures in billion-scale urban point clouds, addressing limitations of feature-similarity methods and poor open-vocabulary handling.

Method: Reformulate 3D grounding as structured constraint reasoning; construct query-ready scene graph from urban point clouds; use CodeLLM-driven tools for multimodal evidence on node attributes and spatial relations; model target-context topology with paired hypergraphs; bidirectional topology verification; Reflective Cross-modal Grounding to fuse topology with 2D visual evidence; training-free; CitySTAR-3D benchmark.

Result: CitySTAR improves open-world urban 3D grounding, maintains interpretability and generalization; demonstrates effectiveness across city-scale scenes.

Conclusion: Structured constraint reasoning with cross-modal evidence and topology verification provides robust, interpretable 3D grounding; CitySTAR framework offers a viable path for scalable, open-world grounding in large-scale urban environments; CitySTAR-3D supports broader evaluation and future extensions.

Abstract: 3D grounding aims to localize target entities in complex scenes from natural language and plays a fundamental role in embodied perception and spatial reasoning. However, existing approaches mostly rely on feature similarity or direct matching, making it difficult to connect natural-language intent with the implicit semantic and geometric structures hidden in billion-scale urban point clouds. We reformulate city-scale 3D grounding as structured constraint reasoning, where description semantics are organized into computable cross-modal constraints over open-vocabulary 3D entities, attributes, and spatial relations. We present CitySTAR, a training-free framework for reasoning-driven urban 3D grounding. CitySTAR lifts raw billion-scale urban point clouds into a query-ready scene graph of open-vocabulary 3D instances, with CodeLLM-driven tools supplying multimodal evidence for node attributes and 3D spatial relations. It then models target-context topology with paired hypergraphs and performs bidirectional topology verification for structural disambiguation. Finally, a Reflective Cross-modal Grounding module integrates topology consistency and candidate-centered 2D visual evidence to make decisions over a metric-aware 3D context graph. To further support this setting, we introduce CitySTAR-3D, an enhanced benchmark that improves semantic coverage, instance completeness, bounding-box fidelity, and spatial-relation complexity in city-scale 3D grounding. Extensive experiments show that CitySTAR consistently improves open-world urban 3D grounding while maintaining strong interpretability and generalization.

</details>


### [44] [DirtyMoCap: Robust Motion Capture from Unconstrained Markers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19927)
*Long Wang,Shuting Zhao,Shen Yan,Siyuan Yu,Xiaoben Li,Zeyu Cai,Yumeng Hou,Yuliang Xiu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DirtyMoCap maps unordered, noisy marker observations to a fixed set of proxy anchors (joints and surface points), then fits the SMPL-H model via a differentiable Gauss-Newton solver to recover full-body pose, translation, and shape; achieving robust, layout-free MoCap with fast CUDA optimization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-world optical MoCap data are often sparse, noisy, and unordered with varying configurations, making traditional fixed-layout pipelines fragile. A robust, layout-agnostic pipeline is needed for practical applicability.

Method: 1) Define proxy anchors (skeletal joints and body-surface points). 2) Initialize and track anchors over long sequences with a recurrent sliding-window. 3) Use a differentiable Gauss-Newton solver to fit SMPL-H to anchors, deriving geometric residuals that learn adaptive observation confidence, smoothness, and priors end-to-end. 4) Implement a custom CUDA solver for speed, achieving up to 100x speedups over standard PyTorch. 5) Validate on diverse, noisy marker configurations; demonstrate single-model generalization and apply to heterogeneous raw recordings to produce a Kung Fu motion dataset.

Result: DirtyMoCap outperforms configuration-specific baselines in both joint and vertex reconstruction accuracy across varied layouts; achieves substantial speedups (up to ~100x) with the CUDA solver; generalizes from a single trained model to arbitrary marker configurations; provides a Kung Fu motion dataset and releases code/data.

Conclusion: A robust, generalizable, layout-free MoCap pipeline that integrates end-to-end learned uncertainty and smoothness with a fast, differentiable optimization backend, suitable for real-world, unconstrained marker data.

Abstract: Optical motion capture delivers high-fidelity human motion, but its reliance on strict marker layouts and clean trajectories severely limits its real-world applicability. In practice, tracking systems frequently output unconstrained markers: sparse, noisy, and unordered point clouds with unknown or varying configurations. To bridge the gap between corrupted raw markers and parametric human models, we introduce DirtyMoCap, a robust, marker-layout-free framework. Our core insight is to map unordered marker observations to a fixed set of "proxy anchors" comprising skeletal joints and body surface points, which serve as a stable intermediate representation. We first initialize and track these anchors over long sequences using a recurrent sliding-window architecture. Then, a custom differentiable Gauss-Newton solver fits the SMPL-H model to the tracked anchors to recover full-body pose, translation, and shape. By explicitly deriving geometric residuals, our solver learns adaptive observation confidence, smoothness, and prior weights end-to-end, adapting dynamically to the reliability of the input data. Extensive experiments on diverse, noisy marker configurations demonstrate that DirtyMoCap successfully generalizes across arbitrary layouts using only a single trained model. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art configuration-specific baselines in both joint and vertex reconstruction accuracy, while our custom CUDA solver achieves up to a 100x speedup over standard PyTorch implementations. We further apply DirtyMoCap to heterogeneous raw optical MoCap recordings of traditional Chinese martial arts, yielding a Kung Fu motion dataset of temporally coherent SMPL-H reconstructions. Code and data are available at https://wanglongzju.github.io/DirtyMoCap-Project-Page.

</details>


### [45] [Enhanced Knowledge Distillation for Detection Transformer via Teacher Prediction Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19964)
*Yitong Xing,Yuhao Cheng,Yanping Li,Yichao Yan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TPRD refines teacher predictions in DETR distillation by leveraging stage-wise predictions to provide higher-quality supervision, via Positive Prediction Correction (PPC), Negative Prediction Suppression (NPS), and Maximum Dark Knowledge Preservation (MDKP); this plug-and-play module improves localization/classification signals and preserves dark knowledge, achieving robust gains on COCO and VOC.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: DETRs exhibit stage-wise non-monotonic prediction behavior; relying on a single stage's predictions for distillation leads to degraded positives and overconfident negatives, yielding poor supervision for the student. A refined, stage-aware teacher signal can improve distillation quality.

Method: Introduce Teacher Prediction Refinement Distillation (TPRD), a plug-and-play module that refines teacher outputs before distillation. Positive Prediction Correction (PPC) restores accurate positives from earlier stages to maintain reliable localization/classification signals. Negative Prediction Suppression (NPS) reduces the impact of overconfident negative predictions. Maximum Dark Knowledge Preservation (MDKP) selectively refines target-class logits while preserving non-target relations to maintain dark knowledge.

Result: Extensive experiments on MS COCO and PASCAL VOC show that TPRD improves DETR distillation performance and robustness. Code is released for reproducibility.

Conclusion: TPRD enhances supervision quality for DETR distillation by leveraging stage-wise predictions and preserving dark knowledge; PPC/NPS mitigate degraded positives and overconfident negatives, while MDKP preserves useful dark information, resulting in stronger, more robust detectors.

Abstract: Detection Transformers (DETRs) achieve strong performance in object detection but remain challenging to deploy on edge devices due to their high computational cost. Existing DETR distillation methods mainly focus on aligning distillation points, while largely overlooking the quality of the teacher's supervision itself. We observe that due to stage-wise non-monotonic prediction behavior in DETRs, well-localized or correctly classified predictions from earlier stages may degrade in later ones, and some negative predictions become increasingly overconfident. As a result, relying solely on the current stage's predictions yields inaccurate and inconsistent supervision. To address this issue, we propose Teacher Prediction Refinement Distillation (TPRD), a plug-and-play module that refines teacher predictions before distillation by exploiting stage-wise prediction information. TPRD improves supervision quality through Positive Prediction Correction (PPC), which corrects degraded positive predictions by restoring more accurate ones from earlier stages, ensuring reliable localization and classification signals, and Negative Prediction Suppression (NPS) suppresses the influence of overconfident negatives, preventing them from providing misleading supervision to the student. To preserve informative dark knowledge, we further introduce Maximum Dark Knowledge Preservation (MDKP), which selectively refines target-class logits while retaining non-target relations. Extensive experiments on MS COCO and PASCAL VOC demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. Our code is available at https://github.com/xingyitong1/TPRD.

</details>


### [46] [Beyond the Foreground: FOV-Aware Polyp Image Synthesis via Lesion-Guided Adaptive Mucosal Context Propagation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19966)
*Tong Wang,Yuting He,Bin Ren,Yutong Xie,Guanyu Yang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Foreground-guided diffusion-based polyp image synthesis with lesion-conditioned mucosal context propagation using FOV masking and cross-attention, achieving realistic textures and improved downstream segmentation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Colonoscopy annotations are scarce; existing foreground-guided methods fail due to non-mucosal artefacts and inconsistent mucosal texture/illumination when applied to colonoscopy.

Method: LAMP separates lesion, valid mucosa, and exterior via an FOV mask. It uses lesion-to-mucosa cross-attention to obtain lesion appearance for valid-mucosa locations and FOV-constrained multidirectional Vision Receptance Weighted Key Value propagation to spread this information over legal tissue support, with an adaptive gate fusing residuals into the diffusion U-Net.

Result: On five polyp datasets, LAMP substantially outperforms existing methods in generation quality and consistently improves five downstream segmentation models; code will be released.

Conclusion: LAMP is the first foreground-guided polyp image synthesis framework with adaptive mucosal-context propagation, yielding more realistic, lesion-consistent polyp images and better downstream segmentation.

Abstract: Synthetic image and mask pairs can alleviate scarce colonoscopy annotations, but realistic synthesis requires preserving the supplied lesion while generating compatible mucosa. Existing foreground-guided methods treat all non-foreground pixels as background and rely mainly on local integration. Directly applying them to colonoscopy causes two problems: non-mucosal black regions contaminate generated tissue, and local reasoning produces inconsistent mucosal texture and illumination. We propose LAMP, the first foreground-guided framework for polyp image synthesis based on lesion-guided adaptive mucosal context propagation. LAMP explicitly separates the lesion, valid mucosa, and camera exterior using a field-of-view (FOV) mask. Lesion-to-Mucosa cross-attention extracts lesion appearance conditions for valid-mucosa locations, while FOV-constrained multidirectional Vision Receptance Weighted Key Value propagates them over legal tissue support. An adaptive gate then controls their residual fusion into the diffusion U-Net. Extensive experiments on five polyp datasets demonstrate that LAMP substantially outperforms existing methods in overall generation quality and consistently improves five downstream segmentation models. Our code will be released at https://github.com/wangtong627/LAMP.

</details>


### [47] [An Event Preserving Velocity Invariant Representation for Event Cameras](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19973)
*Mikihiro Ikura,Luna Gava,Jiahang Wu,Chiara Bartolozzi,Arren Glover*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SCARF provides a real-time, velocity-invariant, event-preserving representation for event cameras, outperforming prior methods in efficiency and representation quality.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution via asynchronous pixels but pose algorithmic challenges. Many velocity-invariant approaches discard temporal information by turning events into image-like representations, limiting performance under varying motion.

Method: Introduce Set of Centre Active Receptive Fields (SCARF), a representation that preserves raw events while maintaining velocity invariance across fast motion, stationary scenes, and independently moving objects.

Result: SCARF achieves state-of-the-art performance in both computational efficiency and representation quality on relevant benchmarks.

Conclusion: SCARF provides a robust, real-time, velocity-invariant event representation that preserves raw events and handles diverse motion regimes effectively.

Abstract: Event cameras provide low-latency, high temporal resolution perception for real-time vision tasks such as robotics.The novel circuitry (i.e. asynchronous, independent pixels) that enables these advantages also introduces new algorithmic challenges. Velocity-invariant representations alleviate missing observations under slow motion and motion blur under fast motion, but most discard temporal information by converting events into image-like representations. We propose Set of Centre Active Receptive Fields (SCARF), a real-time velocity-invariant representation that preserves raw events while consistently handling fast motion, stationary scenes, and independently moving objects. SCARF achieves state-of-the-art performance in both computational efficiency and representation quality.

</details>


### [48] [QCPruner: Query-Conditioned Population Coverage for Visual Token Pruning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19990)
*Shengli He,Yongchao Liang,Roumeng He,Junjie Zeng,Jiyuan He,Can Wu,Li Zheng*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: QCPruner is a training-free, query-conditioned token pruning method for multimodal LLMs that uses bilateral utility weighting with keyword anchors to select visual targets and candidate representations under a nonnegative, monotone submodular facility-location objective, achieving strong pruning performance without model updates.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The large visual-token load in multimodal LLMs drives the need for pruning to reduce computation, but pruning must preserve query-relevant evidence and avoid redundancy within a fixed budget. Existing methods lack a shared per-visual query utility to weight targets and candidates, motivating a unified, query-conditioned approach.

Method: QCPruner uses keyword-matched query anchors to fuse cross-modal cues into a query-conditioned utility. It applies this utility to both visual targets and candidate representatives within a visual-affinity-based coverage framework. The resulting objective is a nonnegative facility-location function that is monotone and submodular, enabling a (1-1/e) greedy guarantee and requiring no model training or parameter updates.

Result: Across LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-Video, and Qwen2.5-VL, QCPruner achieves the highest average relative performance among evaluated complete-system pruning methods at every reported token budget. At 32 of 576 tokens on LLaVA-1.5-7B, it retains 96.1% of unpruned performance vs 93.9% for the best baseline; at 256 of 1296 tokens on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, it retains 96.7% vs 92.5%.

Conclusion: QCPruner offers a principled, training-free pruning framework with query-conditioned bilateral utility that achieves state-of-the-art relative performance across multiple MLLM systems, maintaining most of the unpruned accuracy at practical token budgets and benefiting from a monotone submodular optimization guarantee.

Abstract: The high visual-token load in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) motivates training-free pruning to reduce later-layer computation, but under a fixed budget, pruning must preserve query-relevant evidence while avoiding redundancy. Existing methods rank tokens, diversify selected subsets, or optimize coverage without using a shared per-visual query utility to weight both visual targets and candidate representatives. We introduce QCPruner, which makes both roles query-conditioned through bilateral utility weighting. Using keyword-matched query anchors, QCPruner fuses two cross-modal cues into utility and applies it to both visual targets and candidate representatives within visual-affinity-based coverage. The resulting nonnegative facility-location objective is monotone and submodular, retains the standard (1-1/e) greedy guarantee, and requires no model training or parameter updates. Across LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-Video, and Qwen2.5-VL, QCPruner achieves the highest average relative performance among evaluated complete-system pruning methods at every reported token budget. At 32 of 576 tokens on LLaVA-1.5-7B, it retains 96.1% of unpruned performance, versus 93.9% for the strongest evaluated baseline. At 256 of 1296 tokens on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, the corresponding values are 96.7% and 92.5%.

</details>


### [49] [AVTrace: Diagnosing Audio-Visual Temporal Reasoning in Omni Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19991)
*Longyin Zhang,Parth Sakhare Mahendra,Chengwei Wei,Ning Zhang,Lim Ming Chong,Sirui He,Ai Ti Aw*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: AVTrace introduces a silver-standard diagnostic suite for temporal reasoning in audiovisual models; results show current omni models struggle with synchronization, chain parsing, and event-conditioned grounding; temporal post-training offers gains; text overlap is not indicative of temporal localization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Assess and diagnose the temporal reasoning capabilities of open omni models beyond semantic text overlap.
